narrative.summary: Iran governs AI mainly through the Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution, which on 29 Khordad 1403 (18 June 2024) created a National AI Steering Council and a National AI Organization under the President, and adopted the National AI Document, Iran's AI strategy and ethics framework with a horizon to 2033. In 2025 the government set up a Headquarters for the Development of AI Technology and Applications, and the communications regulator created a licence for AI service providers, with fees set by the Cabinet. An earlier draft National AI Development Roadmap was published by the ICT ministry's research institute in October 2022. Iran has no general data protection law; a personal data protection bill is pending.

instruments.summary: Single-article resolution of the Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution that endorses the outline of the National AI Document and delegates approval of its detailed provisions to the Council's standing council (shora-ye mo'in). It creates a National AI Steering Council chaired by the President to plan, coordinate and oversee implementation, and establishes the National Artificial Intelligence Organization as an independent body under the President whose head acts as the steering council's secretary. A note tasks the Vice-Presidency for Science, Technology and Knowledge-Based Economy with drafting the organization's statute within three months for approval.

instruments.summary: Draft national roadmap for AI development prepared by the AI Innovation and Development Centre of the ICT Research Institute, with input from academia, industry and the private sector, using the methodology of the Supreme Council of Science, Research and Technology. It sets a vision, macro policies, values and strategies with actions, programmes and projects in two parts: developing AI applications in priority areas such as health, transport, agriculture, education, industry and the environment, and building enablers such as specialised human resources, infrastructure, standards, data release and legal and ethical issues.

instruments.current_status: Approved at session 483 of the Council of Assistants of the Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution under a delegation from the Council's 901st session of 29 Khordad 1403 (18 June 2024), and communicated for implementation by the acting President as chair of the Council; binding from communication. Listed as in force in the national laws and regulations system.
instruments.summary: Iran's national AI strategy, with a vision to 1412 (2033). It defines AI and AI ethics, sets value principles grounded in Islamic values (including privacy and data security, justice and human dignity, preventing AI being used for domination, and avoiding social isolation), and sets strategic policies, national strategies and measures covering governance infrastructure (technical, legal, regulatory and standards), data and computing, skills, research and priority application areas. The Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution oversees implementation, the National AI Steering Council coordinates it and the National AI Organization under the President runs the AI ecosystem; the government must fund the Organization through a separate budget line.

instruments.summary: Cabinet decision setting up a cross-government Headquarters for the Development of AI Technology and Applications to coordinate AI policy and avoid duplication between ministries. Its stated vision is for Iran to rank first in South-West Asia and among the world's top ten countries in AI. The Headquarters coordinates and supports state bodies and the private sector to build knowledge, skills and computing infrastructure, improve data production, security and sharing, support knowledge-based AI businesses, promote public AI literacy, expand international cooperation and encourage AI exports.

instruments.summary: Regulation creating a licence for AI service providers (AISP), issued by the Communications Regulatory Authority. Licensed companies may offer AI as a service at infrastructure, platform and software levels, including pre-trained models for language, image and speech processing, analytics, automated or semi-automated decision systems, AI content generation and model development platforms, as well as AI quality, ethics, transparency and safety services. Applicants must be non-state companies registered in Iran with foreign shareholding of at most 49%, post a bank guarantee and provide at least 200 petaflops of computing within the one-year preliminary approval. The decision sets licence duties, a security annex overseen by the Ministry of Intelligence, and graded penalties up to suspension and revocation.

instruments.summary: Government decree setting the fees for the AI service provider (AISP) licence. As amended in April 2026, applicants pay a licence fee of 500 billion rials to the treasury when the licence is issued, and licence holders pay 3% of their audited annual revenue as the government's share. It also sets a table of penalties for breaches of licence obligations, from warnings and fines as a share of revenue to suspension and revocation.

coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): This review was carried out on 12 October 2026, but official Iranian websites could not be accessed: every government, parliament and gazette site refused the connection. The one recorded document could therefore only be located, not read, and the reported 2026 AI law and the National AI Document are listed as leads. Iran is marked for a later retry.

Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. All Iranian official hosts (sccr.ir, rc.majlis.ir, qavanin.ir, rrk.ir, isti.ir, ict.gov.ir, president.ir, ai.gov.ir) failed with curl (reset) and WebFetch (503/502). The single record (SCCR resolution 236) is located only from the search engine's indexed copy of the official page; its adoption event was dropped because the date was not read on the source. Iran is not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: Searched for Majlis laws and bills on AI (National AI Development Law 2026, Seventh Development Plan Law Art. 65(c)) and the data protection bill; rc.majlis.ir, qavanin.ir and rrk.ir unreachable, so held as leads.; Government: Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution (resolution no. 236 recorded, located only; National AI Document held as lead), presidency and Vice-Presidency for Science and Technology (National AI Organization); sccr.ir, president.ir, isti.ir unreachable.; Ministries: Searched ICT (draft roadmap lead), health/medical ethics, education, administrative and recruitment organisation: no official AI document text located; sites unreachable.; Regulators: No data protection authority exists; searched cyber/passive defence, central bank and telecom regulator AI documents: searched, nothing found.. Not reached: All Iranian official hosts (sccr.ir, rc.majlis.ir, qavanin.ir, rrk.ir, isti.ir, ict.gov.ir, president.ir, ai.gov.ir) unreachable by curl and WebFetch; no document text could be read; Ministry-level AI documents (health, education, justice, defence, finance) not checkable on their sites; Central Bank of Iran, CRA (telecom regulator), AFTA/passive defence AI documents. Could not verify: sccr.ir/pro/3432 (resolution no. 236); National AI Document official text; National AI Development Law official text and dates; Seventh Plan Law Art. 65(c) wording; ICT ministry draft AI roadmap page. binding-law, ethics, risk-assurance, public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, data-privacy, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.

Record as binding_law once the official text (Majlis law database or Official Gazette) is read. Earlier: 'طرح ملی هوش مصنوعی' general outline approved 28 Ordibehesht 1404. Update 2026-10-18: rechecked; the Majlis research centre site (rc.majlis.ir) refused the connection, the national laws portal qavanin.ir answered only with a redirect/error page, and rrk.ir timed out; the official presidency site search found no text of the law. Still a lead. 2026-10-22: not yet listed in the national laws and regulations system (qavanin.ir title search for AI); rc.majlis.ir did not load in a desktop browser.
